newsitem.title: FRANCE: Appeal will not delay Thomson CSF sale-govt.
newsitem.headline: Appeal will not delay Thomson CSF sale-govt.

text.p: The French Finance Ministry said on Thursday that privatisation of Thomson-CSF would go ahead as planned despite a legal appeal over an aborted attempt to sell off its parent Thomson SA.

Lagardere Groupe has appealed a ruling by the Privatisation Commission which prompted the government to reverse an earlier decision to sell Thomson SA to Lagardere and South Korea's Daewoo Electronics.

"This appeal will in no way have an effect on the current procedure to privatise Thomson," a Finance Ministry spokeswoman said. "The prime minister (Alain Juppe) will, as scheduled, announce a decision on the Thomson-CSF sale before the end of February."
Under the aborted deal, Lagardere would have bought Thomson-CSF, a defence electronics company, and Daewoo would have taken the parent company's other unit, Thomson Multimedia (TMM).
After the government decision to suspend privatisation of Thomson SA, which provoked anger in South Korea, the government instead decided to sell off the two subsidiaries separately.

Industry analysts said the Lagardere appeal could hurt its position in the race for Thomson-CSF. "They have been lagging behind recently after Alcatel said it was teaming up with Aerospatiale and Dassault Aviation," one French analyst said.
